plan: Final experiment design submitted as the message body above. The document covers: (a) rationale anchored to the two halves of the research question and how the design tests each; (b) full factor grid method × M × P with explicit per-method M floors and ZB-2p infeasible cells documented (not silently dropped); (c) constant-b framing stated explicitly with B = M·b by design, single GPT-style transformer, identical precision and optimizer sharding, software-stack pin; (d) measurement protocol with W_warmup_mb = ceil((5·P)/M)·M and W_measure_mb = max(50·M, microbatches for ≥ 10s wall clock), ≥ 3 seeds per cell, mean ± 95% CI; (e) analysis plan with throughput-vs-M curves, T(M) = T_inf·M/(M+M_0) saturation fit reporting T_inf and M_0, cross-method ranking at matched smallest feasible M with bootstrap CIs, mixed-model interaction test throughput ~ M·method with seed random effects and ZB-2p-vs-others slope contrast, gap-to-peak T(M)/T(M_max) diagnostic, plus falsification checks; (f) feasibility section that explicitly states no code was executed, /workspace contained only task.json, GPU and network are disabled, dependencies not preinstalled, and every repo-specific knob is documented as an assumption to confirm; (g) decision log with 14 reversible decisions plus standing assumptions A1-A6 and standing uncertainties U1-U6. No numerical results are claimed. No repo paths, flags, or schedule names are fabricated. The closing "What this design does NOT claim" block enumerates the negative claims explicitly.

context.question: Does the throughput for methods 1F1B, 1F1B-I, and ZB-1p improve as the number of microbatches increases, while ZB-2p maintains high throughput even with fewer microbatches? (Note: These methods are implemented as part of the zero bubble pipeline parallelism strategies in this repository, which aim to reduce pipeline bubbles and maintain high throughput.)
